title: CompositeLipschitzHessian.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Minimize f(x)+ψ(x) over a convex domain. The function f is globally convex and twice continuously differentiable; ψ is convex on the domain. A global minimizer xstar exists.

problem_class.label: composite
problem_class.details: The smooth component f is accessed through derivatives. The potentially nonsmooth component ψ and domain are accessed through exact regularized model minimization. Extending ψ by +∞ outside the domain gives a proper closed convex function.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Oracle 0 returns ∇f(x) exactly at every queried point, for every call index and seed.

oracle.label: proximal
oracle.details: Oracle 2 exactly minimizes ⟨b,z−c⟩+½⟨z−c,Q(z−c)⟩+(a/3)‖z−c‖³+sψ(z) over the domain. Valid queries require s>0, a≥0, symmetric positive-semidefinite Q, and either a>0 or positive-definite Q. The returned point satisfies the specified variational inequality. No function-value oracle is supplied.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Oracle 1 returns the full exact Hessian ∇²f(x), represented as a continuous linear operator. Its calls are budgeted separately from gradient and model-solver calls.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its induced norm. No dimension bound is imposed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The Hessian obeys ‖∇²f(x)−∇²f(y)‖≤H‖x−y‖ globally. Public inputs are E, x0, H>0, R>0, ε>0, and integer m≥1. The feasible starting point satisfies ‖x0−xstar‖≤R. The functions, domain, and minimizer are hidden instance data. No global gradient-Lipschitz bound, bounded domain, or strong convexity is assumed.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CompositeLipschitzHessian.lean: Params, Problem, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, spec.admissible.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output x must satisfy f(x)+ψ(x)−(f(xstar)+ψ(xstar))≤ε.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The returned point must belong to the domain.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: Feasibility and the objective-gap bound hold almost surely under the joint algorithm and oracle seed law, within fixed separate oracle budgets.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: This is standard finite-dimensional composite convex optimization with a Lipschitz Hessian and idealized exact regularized-model solves. Separate oracle budgets specify the complexity accounting.

descriptionHtml:
Composite Minimization with Lipschitz Hessian

We consider minimizing F=f+ψ over a convex set D in a finite-dimensional real inner product space E. The function f:E→R is convex and twice continuously differentiable, with H-Lipschitz Hessian, where H>0; ψ:E→R is convex on D and has a closed epigraph restricted to D. A given point x0∈D satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R for a minimizer x⋆∈D and R>0. Three oracles return exact gradients, exact Hessians, and exact composite model solutions. For ε>0, the goal is x¯∈D with F(x¯)−F(x⋆)≤ε almost surely under P, the joint law of algorithm and oracle randomness.

Write F(x)=f(x)+ψ(x). The optimization problem is minx∈DF(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ on E, and ∥⋅∥op denotes the induced operator norm. The algorithm receives E, x0, H>0, R>0, ε>0, and an integer m≥1.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convex composite objective). The function f is convex on E, the set D⊆E is convex, and ψ is convex on D. In particular, for t∈[0,1], f((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)f(x)+tf(y),x,y∈E,ψ((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)ψ(x)+tψ(y),x,y∈D. The restricted epigraph {(x,r)∈E×R:x∈D, ψ(x)≤r} is closed in E×R.

Assumption 2 (Lipschitz Hessian). The function f is twice continuously Fréchet differentiable on E. Its Hessian, viewed as a linear operator from E to E, satisfies ∥∇2f(x)−∇2f(y)∥op≤H∥x−y∥,x,y∈E.

Assumption 3 (Minimizer and initial distance). The given starting point x0 and a minimizer x⋆ belong to D, with F(x⋆)≤F(x)for every x∈D,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R.

Gradient and Hessian queries may be made at any x∈E. The gradient oracle returns ∇f(x) at x, and the Hessian oracle returns ∇2f(x) at x.

The third oracle solves composite models. A model query consists of a center c∈E, a vector a∈E, a linear operator B:E→E, a cubic coefficient γ≥0, and a scale s>0. The operator must satisfy ⟨u,Bv⟩=⟨Bu,v⟩for all u,v∈E,⟨u,Bu⟩≥0for all u∈E. In addition, either γ>0, or there exists μ>0 such that ⟨u,Bu⟩≥μ∥u∥2,u∈E. For every such query, the model oracle returns a point z∈D satisfying the exact variational inequality d(z)=a+B(z−c)+γ∥z−c∥(z−c),0≤⟨d(z),u−z⟩+s(ψ(u)−ψ(z)),u∈D. Equivalently, z minimizes over D the model M(x)=⟨a,x−c⟩+12⟨x−c,B(x−c)⟩+γ3∥x−c∥3+sψ(x). The model guarantee holds for every valid query and every oracle reply, including queries chosen using previous replies. Gradient, Hessian, and model-solution calls are counted separately.

After the allotted calls, the output must satisfy x¯∈D,F(x¯)−F(x⋆)≤εP-a.s. Under the joint law P, the algorithm’s randomness is independent of the oracle’s randomness.

comparisonHtml:
In a finite-dimensional real inner-product space E, f∈C2(E) is convex and ∥∇2f(x)−∇2f(y)∥≤H∥x−y∥ globally. The function ψ is convex on C with closed epigraph over C; x0,x⋆∈C, x⋆ minimizes F=f+ψ on C, and ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R. Parameters H,R,ε>0 and integer m≥1 are supplied. Oracles provide exact gradients, Hessians, and exact convex cubic/positive-definite quadratic composite model solves. Target: a feasible x with F(x)−F(x⋆)≤ε almost surely.

(2) A-NPE (Monteiro and Svaiter 2013), Thms. 6.4, 7.15 (2012 revision) O(m(1+T2/7)ℓ) (1): at m=T1/3→∞, O(T1/3log4⁡(2+T)) instead of O(T13/21ℓ). Requires gradients/model solves costing 1/m of Hessians; no gain at m=1. (1) needs global smoothness, exact cubic solves rather than inexact quadratic solves; up to m1/7+m/T2/7 more solves, ignoring logs (T≥1).
(3) (Zhang et al. 2026), Thm. 4.1, v1 (preprint) O((m+m1/7T2/7)log11/3⁡(2+m)) (1) extends (3) from ψ=0, C=E to closed convex composite objectives using exact composite model solves; matches polynomial dependence on the overlap. (1) loses a factor log1/3⁡(2+m)log⁡(2+T/m3) on the overlap, with much larger explicit constants.
(4) CALEN (Chen et al. 2026), Thm. 5.1, v3 O((m+m13/21T2/7)log⁡(2+m)), m≥2 (1) extends (4) from ψ=0, C=E to composite objectives. On the overlap: m1/7 instead of m13/21 in the accuracy term, before logarithms; (3) already attains this power. (1) adds logarithmic overhead and much larger explicit constants; the improved power does not imply uniform total-cost dominance.

Abbr: T=HR3/ε; ℓ=1+|log⁡ε|+|log⁡H|+|log⁡R|. Costs are G+M+mH, where G,M,H count gradient, composite model, and Hessian calls, including inner iterations and search trials. For ψ=0, C=E, model solutions use only query data and are internal computation, so oracle cost is G+mH. Logarithms are natural.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Defs
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.FiniteDimension

namespace LongTails.Setups.CompositeLipschitzHessian

open OracleTemplate MeasureTheory Set
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

structure Params where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [innerE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  x0 : E
  H : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  m : ℕ

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.innerE Params.finiteE

structure Problem (p : Params) where
  f : p.E → ℝ
  ψ : p.E → ℝ
  domain : Set p.E
  xstar : p.E

structure Model (p : Params) where
  center : p.E
  linear : p.E
  quadratic : p.E →L[ℝ] p.E
  cubic : ℝ
  scale : ℝ

def Model.valid {p : Params} (q : Model p) : Prop :=
  0 < q.scale ∧ 0 ≤ q.cubic ∧
    (∀ x y, ⟪x, q.quadratic y⟫ = ⟪q.quadratic x, y⟫) ∧
    (∀ x, 0 ≤ ⟪x, q.quadratic x⟫) ∧
    (0 < q.cubic ∨ ∃ μ : ℝ, 0 < μ ∧ ∀ x, μ * ‖x‖ ^ 2 ≤ ⟪x, q.quadratic x⟫)

noncomputable def Model.derivative {p : Params} (q : Model p) (z : p.E) : p.E :=
  q.linear + q.quadratic (z - q.center) +
    (q.cubic * ‖z - q.center‖) • (z - q.center)

def Model.solution {p : Params} (q : Model p) (F : Problem p) (z : p.E) : Prop :=
  z ∈ F.domain ∧ ∀ u ∈ F.domain,
    0 ≤ ⟪q.derivative z, u - z⟫ + q.scale * (F.ψ u - F.ψ z)

abbrev spec : Setup where
  numOracles := 3
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := Problem p
  Query p := p.E ⊕ Model p
  Reply p := p.E ⊕ (p.E →L[ℝ] p.E)
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid p := 0 < p.H ∧ 0 < p.R ∧ 0 < p.ε ∧ 1 ≤ p.m
  admissible p F O :=
    ContDiff ℝ 2 F.f ∧ ConvexOn ℝ univ F.f ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖fderiv ℝ (gradient F.f) x - fderiv ℝ (gradient F.f) y‖ ≤
      p.H * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    ConvexOn ℝ F.domain F.ψ ∧
    IsClosed {z : p.E × ℝ | z.1 ∈ F.domain ∧ F.ψ z.1 ≤ z.2} ∧
    p.x0 ∈ F.domain ∧ F.xstar ∈ F.domain ∧ ‖p.x0 - F.xstar‖ ≤ p.R ∧
    (∀ x ∈ F.domain, F.f F.xstar + F.ψ F.xstar ≤ F.f x + F.ψ x) ∧
    (∀ k x seed, O.answer k (0, Sum.inl x) seed = Sum.inl (gradient F.f x)) ∧
    (∀ k x seed, O.answer k (1, Sum.inl x) seed =
      Sum.inr (fderiv ℝ (gradient F.f) x)) ∧
    (∀ k q seed, q.valid → ∃ z,
      O.answer k (2, Sum.inr q) seed = Sum.inl z ∧ q.solution F z)
  successful p F output P := ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure _),
    output ω ∈ F.domain ∧ F.f (output ω) + F.ψ (output ω) -
      (F.f F.xstar + F.ψ F.xstar) ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.CompositeLipschitzHessian
